data.content_ref: inline:The target answers a different question than the one asked. The problem asks under what conditions a test CONSTRAINS its subject rather than describes it, and asks for an account of the observed asymmetry: compile.py — the one module installed under shown-to-fail-first — is the ONLY module that lost a mutation (1/9), while every ordinarily-guarded module kept 4/4 to 6/7. The expected reading is that shown-to-fail-first installation is what makes a test constrain (it forces the test to have teeth before the subject exists), whereas tests written after the subject merely describe it. The target instead asserts the survival count is 'dominated by arbitrary registry entries that were never exercised by any test' and is 'consistent with registry-size and coverage variance, not with a shown-to-fail mechanism'. But the record's own distribution contradicts a generic coverage/confound reading: compile.py is the site of the ONLY mutation loss in the entire record (1 total loss across 26 mutations), and it is also the only module installed fail-first. A confound that predicts uniform noise across one author's one-week repository cannot explain why the loss concentrates exactly and exclusively at the module with the distinctive installation ritual. The target never engages this co-location — the most probative fact in the record — and its counterconditions only test peripheral versions of the confound (e.g., whether the 1/9 mutation is 'in a directly tested code path'), not the core anomaly that the sole fail-first module is the sole site of constraint. It thus refutes a mechanism the distribution actually supports.
